question: Which of the following shows the strongest force of attraction between particles?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Iron rod.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Matter exists mainly in three states — solid, liquid and gas — and the difference between them comes from the strength of the intermolecular force of attraction and the space between particles. (अंतराणविक आकर्षण बल — ठोस में सर्वाधिक)

 

• In solids like an iron rod, the particles are packed very close together and the force of attraction between them is the strongest of the three states, which is why solids have a fixed shape and volume.

 

• Liquids (alcohol, water) have moderate intermolecular force — enough to keep a fixed volume but not a fixed shape. Gases (oxygen) have the weakest force of attraction, so they expand to fill any container.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Order of intermolecular force of attraction: Solid > Liquid > Gas; order of intermolecular space is the reverse: Gas > Liquid > Solid.

 

• Change of state due to change in temperature/pressure is a physical change; no new substance is formed.

 

• The kinetic energy of particles increases in the order Solid < Liquid < Gas, which is opposite to the force of attraction.

 

NOTE

 

• Alcohol (Option A): A liquid; moderate intermolecular force, weaker than a solid.

 

• Water (Option B): A liquid; particles can slide past each other, unlike a rigid solid.

 

• Oxygen gas (Option D): A gas; particles are far apart with negligible force of attraction.

question: What does the area under a velocity-time graph give?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Displacement.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• On a velocity-time (v-t) graph, the area enclosed between the graph line and the time axis gives the displacement covered by the object in that time interval. (वेग-समय ग्राफ का क्षेत्रफल — विस्थापन)

 

• This follows from the definition velocity = displacement/time, so displacement = velocity × time, which is exactly what the area of the v-t graph (a rectangle, triangle or trapezium, depending on the motion) represents.

 

• The slope (gradient) of a velocity-time graph, by contrast, gives the acceleration of the object, since acceleration = change in velocity/time.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• On a distance-time graph, the slope gives speed; a straight line indicates uniform speed and a curved line indicates changing speed.

 

• On an acceleration-time graph, the area under the graph gives the change in velocity.

 

• A horizontal line on a v-t graph means the object moves with constant (uniform) velocity, i.e., zero acceleration.

 

NOTE

 

• Acceleration (Option B): Obtained from the slope, not the area, of a v-t graph.

 

• Force (Option C): Obtained using Newton's second law, F = ma; not directly read off a v-t graph.

 

• Work done (Option D): Obtained from the area under a force-displacement graph, not a velocity-time graph.

question:
A convex lens is thicker at the middle compared to the edges. Due to this

shape, how does it affect parallel light rays passing through it?
option_1: It causes the rays to reflect back along the same path
option_2: It causes the rays to meet at a point, performing a converging action
option_3: It causes the rays to spread out, performing a diverging action
option_4: It causes the rays to scatter randomly
solution_text:
The correct answer is It causes the rays to meet at a point, performing a converging action.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A convex lens is thicker at the centre and thinner at the edges. Because of this shape, parallel rays of light passing through it are refracted (bent) inward and made to meet (converge) at a single point called the principal focus. (उत्तल लेंस — अभिसारी लेंस)

 

• This converging behaviour is why a convex lens is also called a converging lens. The distance between the optical centre and the principal focus is the focal length.

 

• A convex lens can form both real and virtual images depending on the position of the object — real, inverted images when the object is beyond the focus, and a virtual, magnified image (as in a magnifying glass) when the object is within the focal length.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• A concave lens is thinner at the middle and thicker at the edges; it causes parallel rays to spread out (diverge) and is called a diverging lens.

 

• Convex lenses are used in magnifying glasses, cameras, projectors, telescopes, and to correct hypermetropia (long-sightedness).

 

• Refraction, not reflection, is the phenomenon responsible for a lens bending light; reflection is what happens at a mirror.

 

NOTE

 

• Reflects back along the same path (Option A): Describes what happens at a plane mirror with light incident normally, not a lens.

 

• Spreads out, diverging (Option C): This is the behaviour of a concave lens, not a convex lens.

 

• Scatter randomly (Option D): Describes diffuse reflection from a rough surface, not the action of a lens.

question:
Why do recessive traits like 't' for dwarfness in pea plants only show up when both

alleles are recessive?
option_3: Recessive alleles cannot be passed on.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dominant alleles mask recessive alleles.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Mendelian genetics, when an organism has two different alleles for a trait (heterozygous, e.g. Tt), the dominant allele (T for tallness) expresses itself and masks (suppresses) the effect of the recessive allele (t for dwarfness). (प्रभावी व अप्रभावी युग्मविकल्पी)

 

• A recessive trait such as dwarfness can only appear in the phenotype when the organism is homozygous recessive (tt) — i.e., it has received the recessive allele from both parents, so there is no dominant allele present to mask it.

 

• This masking effect is the basis of Mendel's Law of Dominance, one of the three laws he formulated from his pea plant experiments.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gregor Mendel, the 'Father of Genetics', conducted his experiments on the garden pea (Pisum sativum) because it has easily distinguishable contrasting traits and normally self-pollinates.

 

• Mendel proposed three laws: Law of Dominance, Law of Segregation and Law of Independent Assortment.

 

• A Punnett square is used to predict the possible genotype and phenotype combinations of offspring from a genetic cross.

 

NOTE

 

• Recessive alleles are stronger (Option B): Incorrect — it is the dominant allele that is expressed over the recessive one, not the other way round.

 

• Recessive alleles cannot be passed on (Option C): Incorrect — recessive alleles are passed on normally; they simply remain hidden (unexpressed) in heterozygous individuals.

 

• Recessive alleles are never expressed (Option D): Incorrect — they are expressed whenever the organism is homozygous recessive (tt).

question: The poultry birds grown for the purpose of meat production are called _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Broilers.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In poultry farming, birds reared specifically for meat production are called broilers, while birds reared for egg production are called layers. (ब्रॉयलर — मांस हेतु पाले गए मुर्गे)

 

• Broiler breeds are selected and fed to gain body weight quickly in a short period (usually 6-7 weeks), giving tender, high-quality meat.

 

• Layers, by contrast, are managed and fed to maximise egg-laying capacity over a longer productive life rather than for fast weight gain.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Poultry farming is the practice of rearing domestic fowl (hens, ducks, turkeys) for both eggs and meat, and is an important branch of animal husbandry.

 

• Good management of a poultry farm includes proper housing, nutritious feed, hygienic conditions and disease prevention (vaccination).

 

• Cross-breeding between indigenous (e.g. Aseel, Kadaknath) and foreign breeds (e.g. Leghorn, Rhode Island Red) is done to combine desirable traits like disease resistance with high productivity.

 

NOTE

 

• Layers (Option A): Birds specifically raised for egg production, not meat.

 

• Fowls (Option C): A general term for domestic birds (including hens); it does not specifically denote meat-producing birds.

 

• Cocks (Option D): Refers to adult male birds; it is not a term for a category reared specifically for meat.

question:
If a porter carrying a load on his head moves on a horizontal road with uniform speed,

the work done by the gravitational force on the load:
solution_text:
The correct answer is is zero.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Work done, W = F × d × cosθ, where θ is the angle between the direction of the force and the direction of displacement. (कार्य = बल × विस्थापन × cosθ)

 

• The gravitational force on the load acts vertically downward, while the porter's displacement is entirely horizontal (along the road). The angle between them is θ = 90°.

 

• Since cos 90° = 0, the work done by gravity on the load is W = F × d × cos90° = 0, regardless of the distance walked or the weight of the load.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Work is a scalar quantity, measured in joules (J) in the SI system; 1 joule = 1 newton × 1 metre.

 

• Work is positive when force and displacement are in the same direction (θ = 0°), negative when they are opposite (θ = 180°, e.g. friction), and zero when they are perpendicular (θ = 90°).

 

• Common zero-work situations: a person holding a heavy bag while standing still (no displacement) and a satellite moving in a circular orbit (gravity always perpendicular to velocity).

 

NOTE

 

• Cannot be determined (Option A): Incorrect — the geometry (horizontal motion under vertical gravity) is enough to fix the angle at 90°, so the work can be determined exactly.

 

• Is maximum (Option C): Work is maximum when force and displacement are parallel (θ = 0°), which is not the case here.

 

• Is minimum (Option D): While zero is indeed the minimum possible value, describing it simply as 'zero' (as gravity is perpendicular to displacement) is the precise physical reason, matching Option B.

question: Which of the following statements about ethanol is correct?
option_2: Ethanol does not dissolve in water.
option_3: Ethanol is a liquid with a pleasant smell and is miscible with water.
option_4: Ethanol reacts with sodium to form carbon dioxide.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ethanol is a liquid with a pleasant smell and is miscible with water.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ethanol (C₂H₅OH), commonly called ethyl alcohol, is a colourless, volatile liquid with a pleasant smell, and it is completely miscible (soluble) with water in all proportions. (एथेनॉल — जल में पूर्णतः मिश्रणीय द्रव)

 

• Ethanol belongs to the alcohol homologous series, and its functional group is -OH (hydroxyl). It burns with a clean blue flame and is used as a solvent, in beverages, and as a fuel.

 

• Ethanol reacts with sodium metal to liberate hydrogen gas and form sodium ethoxide: 2Na + 2C₂H₅OH → 2C₂H₅ONa + H₂↑, a reaction used to test for the presence of the -OH group.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Prolonged consumption of ethanol-containing beverages damages the liver and can cause cirrhosis.

 

• Ethanol can be oxidised to ethanoic acid (acetic acid, CH₃COOH), the main component of vinegar, using oxidising agents like alkaline KMnO₄.

 

• Denatured alcohol is ethanol made unfit for drinking by adding poisonous substances like methanol or pyridine, used industrially.

 

NOTE

 

• Non-volatile solid (Option A): Incorrect — ethanol is a volatile liquid, not a solid.

 

• Does not dissolve in water (Option B): Incorrect — ethanol is fully miscible with water due to hydrogen bonding.

 

• Reacts with sodium to form carbon dioxide (Option D): Incorrect — the reaction with sodium releases hydrogen gas, not carbon dioxide.

question: Which of the following cell organelles stores starch, oil and protein granules?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Leucoplast.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Leucoplasts are colourless plastids found in cells not exposed to light (e.g. roots, underground stems, seeds), and they function mainly as storage organelles for starch, oils/fats and proteins. (श्वेतलवक — भंडारण हेतु)

 

• Based on the substance stored, leucoplasts are of three types: amyloplasts (store starch, e.g. in potato), elaioplasts (store oils/fats) and aleuroplasts/proteinoplasts (store proteins).

 

• Plastids are double-membrane-bound organelles found only in plant cells and algae, and are classified into three types based on pigmentation: chloroplast, chromoplast and leucoplast.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chloroplasts contain the green pigment chlorophyll and are the site of photosynthesis. (प्रकाश संश्लेषण)

 

• Chromoplasts contain pigments other than chlorophyll (like carotenoids), giving yellow, orange or red colour to flowers and fruits (e.g. tomato, carrot).

 

• Plastids, like mitochondria, contain their own DNA and ribosomes and are believed to have originated through endosymbiosis.

 

NOTE

 

• All plastids (Option A): Incorrect and too broad — only leucoplasts, not chloroplasts or chromoplasts, specialise in storage of starch/oil/protein.

 

• Chromoplast (Option C): Stores coloured pigments, not starch/oil/protein; responsible for colour in flowers and fruits.

 

• Chloroplast (Option D): The site of photosynthesis, containing chlorophyll; not primarily a storage organelle.

question:
When the same current flows through two wires of equal length but different

resistances, the wire with higher resistance will:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Produce more heat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to Joule's Law of Heating, the heat produced in a conductor is given by H = I²Rt, where I is the current, R the resistance and t the time. (जूल का तापन नियम)

 

• Since heat produced H is directly proportional to resistance R (for the same current I and time t), the wire with the higher resistance will produce more heat than the wire with lower resistance.

 

• This principle is applied practically in heating appliances like electric irons, heaters and geysers, which use high-resistance elements (e.g. nichrome wire) to generate heat efficiently.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Joule's Law of Heating states: heat produced is directly proportional to (i) the square of the current, (ii) the resistance, and (iii) the time for which current flows.

 

• Nichrome, an alloy of nickel and chromium, is used as a heating element because it has high resistance and a high melting point, and does not oxidise easily when red hot.

 

• Fuse wires are made of a metal/alloy with a low melting point (e.g. tin-lead alloy) so they melt and break the circuit when current exceeds a safe limit.

 

NOTE

 

• Produce less heat (Option A): Incorrect — heat is directly, not inversely, proportional to resistance for a given current.

 

• Produce no heat (Option C): Incorrect — any conductor with resistance carrying current produces heat by Joule heating.

 

• Produce the same heat (Option D): Incorrect — since H ∝ R for equal current and time, unequal resistances give unequal heat.

question:
Which of the following wires will have the least resistance if all are made of the same

material?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Short and thick wire.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The resistance of a wire is given by R = ρL/A, where ρ is the resistivity (a material constant), L is the length and A is the cross-sectional area. (प्रतिरोध — लंबाई के अनुक्रमानुपाती, अनुप्रस्थ काट के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती)

 

• Resistance is directly proportional to length (L) — so a shorter wire has less resistance — and inversely proportional to area of cross-section (A) — so a thicker wire (larger A) has less resistance.

 

• Combining both, for wires of the same material, the one that is both short and thick will have the least resistance among the given options.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Resistivity (ρ) depends only on the material and temperature of the conductor, not on its length or area; its SI unit is ohm-metre (Ω·m).

 

• Ohm's Law: V = IR, valid at constant temperature; resistance is measured in ohms (Ω).

 

• Resistance generally increases with temperature for metallic conductors, since increased vibration of atoms hinders electron flow.

 

NOTE

 

• Long and thick wire (Option A): Length increases resistance while thickness decreases it; the net effect is not the minimum among the options.

 

• Short and thin wire (Option B): Shortness decreases resistance but thinness increases it, so this is not the minimum either.

 

• Long and thin wire (Option D): Both length and thinness increase resistance, making this the highest, not lowest, resistance wire.

question:
Which of the following is the irrigation method in which water is tap from deeper strata

by pumps?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tube wells.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A tube well is a deep, narrow well fitted with a pipe from which water is pumped up from deeper strata (groundwater aquifers) using electric or diesel-powered pumps. (नलकूप — भूमिगत जल का दोहन)

 

• Tube wells are a major source of groundwater irrigation in India, especially in states with adequate groundwater like Punjab, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh, and have significantly boosted irrigation coverage since the Green Revolution.

 

• Unlike ordinary dug wells, which tap shallow groundwater and often need manual lifting, tube wells can draw water from much greater depths using mechanised pumping.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sources of irrigation in India are broadly classified as canals, wells/tube wells, tanks and other sources; wells and tube wells together account for the largest share of net irrigated area.

 

• Canal irrigation is prominent in the northern plains (Punjab, Haryana, UP), while tank irrigation is more common in the peninsular plateau (Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu) due to undulating relief and impermeable rocks.

 

• Excessive tube well use can cause over-extraction of groundwater, leading to a falling water table.

 

NOTE

 

• River life system (Option A): Not a standard irrigation term; rivers directly feed canal irrigation systems rather than tapping deep strata.

 

• Rain-fed (Option B): Refers to agriculture that depends directly on rainfall, with no artificial irrigation at all.

 

• Canals (Option D): Draw water from rivers or reservoirs at the surface, not from deep underground strata via pumps.

question:
The phenomenon of change of a liquid into vapour at any temperature below its boiling

point is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is evaporation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Evaporation is the process by which a liquid changes into vapour (gas) at any temperature below its boiling point, occurring only from the surface of the liquid. (वाष्पीकरण — क्वथनांक से नीचे किसी भी ताप पर)

 

• Evaporation is a surface phenomenon caused by the escape of high-energy molecules from the liquid surface, and it causes cooling of the remaining liquid because it takes away latent heat.

 

• Evaporation is faster with increased surface area, higher temperature, lower humidity and greater wind speed — this is why clothes dry faster on a hot, windy day.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Boiling, unlike evaporation, occurs at a fixed temperature (boiling point) and involves bubble formation throughout the bulk of the liquid, not just the surface.

 

• Sublimation is the direct change of a solid into vapour without passing through the liquid state (e.g. camphor, dry ice, naphthalene balls).

 

• Condensation is the reverse of evaporation — the change of vapour into liquid; solidification (freezing) is the change of liquid into solid.

 

NOTE

 

• Solidification (Option A): The change of a liquid into a solid, e.g. water freezing into ice.

 

• Sublimation (Option C): The change of a solid directly into a gas (or vice versa), not liquid to gas.

 

• Condensation (Option D): The change of a gas/vapour into a liquid, the reverse of evaporation.

question:
Read the following statements carefully and select the correct option.

Assertion (A): Decomposition reactions require energy in the form of heat, light, or

electricity.

Reason (R): Energy is absorbed to break down reactant molecules into simpler

products.
option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
option_2: Both A and R are true, and R is not the correct explanation of A.
option_3: A is false, but R is true.
option_4: A is true, but R is false.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A decomposition reaction is a reaction in which a single compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances, and most decomposition reactions are endothermic, requiring energy input in the form of heat, light or electricity. (वियोजन अभिक्रिया — ऊष्माशोषी)

 

• Assertion (A) is true: decomposition reactions do require an external energy source to proceed, since energy must be supplied to break the bonds holding the reactant molecule together.

 

• Reason (R) is true and correctly explains A: the absorbed energy is specifically used to break down the reactant into simpler products, which is exactly why energy input is necessary for decomposition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Types of decomposition reactions based on energy source: thermal decomposition (heat, e.g. CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ on heating limestone), photolytic/photo-decomposition (light, e.g. 2AgCl → 2Ag + Cl₂ in sunlight, used in black-and-white photography) and electrolytic decomposition (electricity, e.g. electrolysis of water into H₂ and O₂).

 

• Decomposition reactions are the opposite of combination reactions, in which two or more substances combine to form a single product.

 

• A common example: heating ferrous sulphate crystals decomposes them into ferric oxide, sulphur dioxide and sulphur trioxide, a reaction accompanied by a characteristic smell.

 

NOTE

 

• Options B, C and D are incorrect because both the assertion and reason are factually correct, and the reason directly explains why the assertion is true (Option B wrongly denies this correct explanation, while C and D wrongly mark one of the statements false).

question: Which of the following elements has atomic number 11?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sodium.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sodium (Na) has atomic number 11, meaning it has 11 protons (and 11 electrons in a neutral atom) in its nucleus. (सोडियम — परमाणु क्रमांक 11)

 

• Its electronic configuration is 2, 8, 1 — it belongs to Group 1 (alkali metals) and Period 3 of the modern periodic table.

 

• Having only one electron in its outermost shell, sodium is highly reactive, readily loses this electron to form a Na⁺ ion, and reacts vigorously with water and air.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Atomic number (Z) = number of protons in the nucleus; it uniquely identifies an element and determines its position in the periodic table (Moseley's law).

 

• Common atomic numbers frequently asked: Hydrogen = 1, Carbon = 6, Nitrogen = 7, Oxygen = 8, Magnesium = 12, Potassium = 19, Calcium = 20.

 

• Alkali metals (Group 1: Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs, Fr) are soft, highly reactive metals stored in kerosene oil to prevent reaction with atmospheric moisture and oxygen.

 

NOTE

 

• Magnesium (Option A): Atomic number 12, a Group 2 alkaline earth metal.

 

• Nitrogen (Option B): Atomic number 7, a non-metal, major constituent of the atmosphere (~78%).

 

• Potassium (Option D): Atomic number 19, another Group 1 alkali metal, symbol K (from Latin *kalium*).

question: A ray of light passing through the principal focus of a convex lens emerges:
solution_text:
The correct answer is parallel to the principal axis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• For a convex lens, a ray of light that passes through (or is directed towards) the principal focus on one side, after refraction, emerges parallel to the principal axis. (उत्तल लेंस के मुख्य फोकस से गुजरने वाली किरण — मुख्य अक्ष के समांतर)

 

• This is one of the standard rules used for ray diagrams with lenses, and it is the exact reverse of the rule that a ray parallel to the principal axis, after refraction, passes through the principal focus.

 

• These two rules, together with the rule that a ray through the optical centre passes undeviated, are used to locate the image formed by a convex lens.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• The three standard rays used to construct ray diagrams for lenses: (i) a ray parallel to the principal axis refracts through the principal focus; (ii) a ray through the principal focus emerges parallel to the axis; (iii) a ray through the optical centre passes straight through without any deviation.

 

• The focal length (f) is the distance between the optical centre and the principal focus; the power of a lens = 1/f (in metres), measured in dioptres (D).

 

• A convex lens has positive power/focal length, while a concave lens has negative power/focal length.

 

NOTE

 

• Back to the source (Option A): Would only happen if the ray struck the lens normally along the axis and reflected, which is not how refraction through a lens works.

 

• Towards the optical centre (Option B): Describes a ray aimed at the optical centre, which instead passes straight through undeviated.

 

• Without deviation (Option C): True only for a ray passing through the optical centre, not one passing through the focus.

question: Which of the following is NOT a trait Mendel studied in pea plants?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Leaf size.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gregor Mendel studied seven contrasting traits in garden pea (*Pisum sativum*) plants: plant height (tall/dwarf), flower position (axial/terminal), flower colour (violet/white), pod shape (inflated/constricted), pod colour (green/yellow), seed shape (round/wrinkled) and seed colour (yellow/green). (मेंडल के सात लक्षण)

 

• Leaf size or leaf-related traits were not among the seven characters Mendel selected for his classic hybridisation experiments.

 

• Mendel chose the pea plant because it has easily distinguishable contrasting traits, a short life cycle, and normally self-pollinates, though it can also be cross-pollinated artificially — features that made it ideal for controlled breeding experiments.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mendel's work, published in 1865 as 'Experiments on Plant Hybridization', was largely ignored during his lifetime and was rediscovered in 1900 by Hugo de Vries, Carl Correns and Erich von Tschermak.

 

• Mendel formulated the Law of Dominance, Law of Segregation and Law of Independent Assortment, laying the foundation of classical genetics.

 

• Mendel is known as the 'Father of Genetics', and his monastery garden experiments used thousands of pea plants over several years.

 

NOTE

 

• Plant height (Option A): One of Mendel's seven traits (tall vs dwarf).

 

• Flower position (Option B): One of Mendel's seven traits (axial vs terminal).

 

• Seed shape (Option D): One of Mendel's seven traits (round vs wrinkled).

question: Which of the following characteristics correctly describes skeletal (striated) muscles?
option_3: Short, cylindrical, branched cells with intercalated discs
option_4: Long, cylindrical, unbranched, multinucleate cells, voluntary control
solution_text:
The correct answer is Long, cylindrical, unbranched, multinucleate cells, voluntary control.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Skeletal (striated/voluntary) muscles are made of long, cylindrical, unbranched fibres that are multinucleate (many nuclei per cell, located at the periphery), and they show alternating light and dark bands (striations). (कंकाल पेशी — बहुकेंद्रकीय, ऐच्छिक)

 

• These muscles are attached to bones by tendons and are under voluntary (willed) control — meaning we can consciously contract or relax them, as in moving the limbs.

 

• They are capable of fast but fatigable contraction, making them suited for quick, powerful movements rather than sustained activity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Smooth (unstriated/involuntary) muscles are spindle-shaped, uninucleate, unstriated, and under involuntary control; found in the walls of internal organs like the stomach, intestines and blood vessels.

 

• Cardiac muscles are branched, uninucleate, striated, and function involuntarily, found only in the heart; they show intercalated discs that help synchronise contraction.

 

• Muscle contraction occurs by the sliding filament theory, involving the proteins actin and myosin.

 

NOTE

 

• Spindle-shaped, uninucleate, involuntary (Option A): Describes smooth muscle, not skeletal muscle.

 

• Branched, uninucleate, involuntary (Option B): Describes cardiac muscle, not skeletal muscle.

 

• Short, cylindrical, branched with intercalated discs (Option C): Also describes cardiac muscle, which is unique in having intercalated discs.

question:
The key difference between rough endoplasmic reticulum and smooth endoplasmic

reticulum is the presence of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is ribosomes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is a network of membranous tubules and sacs in the cytoplasm, and it exists in two forms: Rough ER (RER), which has ribosomes studded on its surface, and Smooth ER (SER), which lacks ribosomes. (खुरदरी अंतर्द्रव्यी जालिका — राइबोसोम युक्त)

 

• Because of the attached ribosomes, RER is the site of protein synthesis — proteins made here are often meant for secretion or for use in membranes.

 

• SER, lacking ribosomes, is instead involved in the synthesis of lipids and steroids, and in detoxification of drugs and poisons (notably abundant in liver cells).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ribosomes themselves are non-membrane-bound organelles made of rRNA and protein, and are the actual site where protein synthesis (translation) occurs, whether free in the cytoplasm or attached to RER.

 

• The cytosol is the fluid matrix of the cytoplasm in which all organelles are suspended — it is common to the whole cell, not a distinguishing feature between RER and SER.

 

• The endoplasmic reticulum is also involved in forming the nuclear envelope and in transporting materials to the Golgi apparatus.

 

NOTE

 

• Cytosol (Option A): The fluid component of the cytoplasm; present throughout the cell, not specific to either type of ER.

 

• Mitochondria (Option C): Separate double-membraned organelles, the 'powerhouse of the cell'; unrelated to distinguishing RER from SER.

 

• Centrosomes (Option D): Organelles involved in organising the spindle fibres during cell division; not related to the ER's structure.

question:
The speed of sound in air is about 343 m/s at room temperature. What happens to its

speed when it travels through water?
solution_text:
The correct answer is It increases.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The speed of sound depends on the density and elasticity of the medium, and in general sound travels fastest in solids, slower in liquids, and slowest in gases. (ध्वनि की चाल — ठोस > द्रव > गैस)

 

• Since water (a liquid) is denser and more elastic than air (a gas), sound travels faster in water than in air — roughly 1,480-1,500 m/s in water compared to about 343 m/s in air at room temperature.

 

• This happens because particles in a denser, more tightly bound medium can transmit vibrations to neighbouring particles more quickly and efficiently than in a sparse gaseous medium.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Speed of sound is even higher in solids — about 5,000-6,000 m/s in steel — because solids have the strongest interparticle bonding of the three states.

 

• The speed of sound in air increases with temperature; it also depends slightly on humidity, but not on the loudness (amplitude) or pitch (frequency) of the sound.

 

• Sound cannot travel through vacuum, since it is a mechanical wave that requires a material medium to propagate.

 

NOTE

 

• Becomes zero (Option A): Incorrect — sound propagates well through water; it is used, for example, in SONAR for underwater detection.

 

• Decreases (Option B): Incorrect — the actual trend is an increase, since water is denser/more elastic than air.

 

• Remains the same (Option D): Incorrect — the speed of sound is medium-dependent and differs significantly between air and water.

question: If the net force on a 10 kg object is zero, its acceleration will be:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 0 m/s².

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to Newton's Second Law of Motion, F = ma, so acceleration a = F/m. (न्यूटन का द्वितीय नियम)

 

• Here, the net force F = 0, so regardless of the object's mass (10 kg) or its speed, the acceleration must be a = 0/10 = 0 m/s².

 

• This is consistent with Newton's First Law (the Law of Inertia): when the net force on a body is zero, the body continues in its state of rest or uniform motion in a straight line — i.e., its velocity stays constant, meaning zero acceleration.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Inertia is the natural tendency of a body to resist a change in its state of rest or motion; mass is a quantitative measure of inertia.

 

• Momentum (p = mv) also remains constant when the net force on a system is zero — this is the basis of the Law of Conservation of Momentum.

 

• A body can move with constant (non-zero) velocity while having zero acceleration, which is exactly the situation here — the object need not be at rest.

 

NOTE

 

• A).8 m/s² (Option A): Any non-zero acceleration would require a non-zero net force by F = ma, which contradicts the given condition of zero net force.

 

• Depends on its velocity (Option C): Incorrect — acceleration depends on net force and mass, not on the object's current velocity.

 

• 10 m/s² (Option D): This would require a net force of 100 N (F = ma = 10×10); with zero net force this value is not possible.

question:
Which of the following terms is used to describe the ability of a plant to recover its lost

parts by growth?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Regeneration.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Regeneration is the ability of an organism to regrow or replace lost or damaged body parts through the growth and development of new cells and tissues. (पुनर्जनन — खोए हुए अंगों की पुनःवृद्धि)

 

• In plants, regeneration is a very common phenomenon — for example, a plant can regrow roots or shoots from a cut stem, and this ability underlies methods of vegetative propagation such as growing a new plant from a cutting.

 

• Regeneration is a form of asexual reproduction when it leads to the formation of a whole new organism from a fragment, and it is especially well developed in simple organisms like planarians, starfish and Hydra, apart from plants.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vegetative propagation, common in plants, includes methods like cutting, grafting, layering and propagation through modified stems/roots (e.g. potato tubers, ginger rhizomes) — all relying on the plant's regenerative capacity.

 

• Totipotency is the property of a plant cell by which it can develop into a complete new organism; it forms the basis of tissue culture.

 

• Animals like the starfish and Hydra are famous examples of high regenerative capacity, able to regrow entire lost body parts.

 

NOTE

 

• Budding (Option A): A form of asexual reproduction (e.g. in Hydra and yeast) in which a new individual develops as an outgrowth (bud) from the parent — not the recovery of a lost part.

 

• Fertilisation (Option B): The fusion of male and female gametes to form a zygote in sexual reproduction, unrelated to regrowth of lost parts.

 

• Binary fission (Option D): A form of asexual reproduction in unicellular organisms where one cell divides into two identical daughter cells.

question: The number of neutrons in an oxygen atom is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 8.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Oxygen has atomic number (Z) = 8 (number of protons) and mass number (A) = 16 (for its most common isotope, O-16). (ऑक्सीजन — 8 प्रोटॉन, 8 न्यूट्रॉन)

 

• Number of neutrons = mass number (A) − atomic number (Z) = 16 − 8 = 8.

 

• For a neutral atom, the number of electrons equals the number of protons; so oxygen has 8 protons, 8 neutrons and 8 electrons.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Atomic number (Z) = number of protons (or electrons in a neutral atom); Mass number (A) = number of protons + number of neutrons.

 

• Isotopes are atoms of the same element (same Z) with different numbers of neutrons (different A) — e.g. Oxygen-16, Oxygen-17 and Oxygen-18 are all isotopes of oxygen.

 

• Oxygen's electronic configuration is 2, 6, with 6 electrons in its outermost shell, making it highly reactive and giving it a valency of 2.

 

NOTE

 

• 16 (Option B): This is the mass number of oxygen (protons + neutrons), not the number of neutrons alone.

 

• 32 (Option C): This is the molecular mass of the diatomic oxygen molecule O₂ (16 × 2), not the neutron count of a single atom.

 

• 7 (Option D): This is the atomic number of nitrogen, not oxygen.

question: An organic compound always contains which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is At least one carbon atom.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Organic compounds are, by definition, compounds of carbon — every organic compound contains at least one carbon atom, usually bonded to hydrogen and often to other elements. (कार्बनिक यौगिक — कार्बन आधारित)

 

• Carbon's unique ability to form strong covalent bonds with itself (a property called catenation) and with other elements allows it to form an enormous variety of chain, branched and ring structures, giving rise to millions of organic compounds.

 

• While many organic compounds also contain hydrogen (and often oxygen, nitrogen, sulphur or halogens), carbon is the one element common to all of them — hydrogen, oxygen or nitrogen are not compulsorily present in every organic compound (e.g. carbon tetrachloride, CCl₄, has no hydrogen).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Inorganic compounds, by contrast, generally do not contain carbon (with a few well-known exceptions like CO₂, CO, carbonates and cyanides, which are treated as inorganic by convention).

 

• Carbon's four valence electrons allow it to form four covalent bonds, giving rise to stable compounds with a wide range of structures — chains, branches and rings.

 

• Organic chemistry is sometimes called the 'chemistry of carbon compounds', and living organisms are built almost entirely from organic molecules like carbohydrates, proteins, fats and nucleic acids.

 

NOTE

 

• Halogens and noble gases (Option A): Neither is essential in organic compounds; many organic compounds contain no halogens at all, and noble gases essentially do not form compounds due to their stable configuration.

 

• Hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen (Option C): These are common in many organic compounds but are not compulsory in every one (e.g. CCl₄ contains no hydrogen, oxygen or nitrogen).

 

• Silicon and phosphorus atoms (Option D): These are not defining or essential constituents of organic compounds at all.

question:
When ester is treated with sodium hydroxide, alcohol and sodium salt of carboxylic

acid is formed. What is the process called?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Saponification.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Saponification is the alkaline hydrolysis of an ester, in which an ester reacts with sodium hydroxide (NaOH) to give an alcohol and the sodium salt of a carboxylic acid (soap). (साबुनीकरण — एस्टर + NaOH → साबुन + ऐल्कोहॉल)

 

• This reaction is the basis of soap manufacture: natural fats/oils (which are esters of long-chain fatty acids with glycerol) are boiled with NaOH solution to produce soap (sodium salts of fatty acids) and glycerol.

 

• The term 'saponification' comes from the Latin word *sapo*, meaning soap, reflecting its central role in soap-making.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Esterification is the reverse reaction — an alcohol reacts with a carboxylic acid (usually with a mineral acid catalyst) to form an ester and water, giving a characteristic sweet/fruity smell.

 

• Soaps are sodium or potassium salts of long-chain fatty acids; they work by forming micelles that trap grease/oil, making it removable with water.

 

• Detergents, unlike soaps, work effectively even in hard water because their calcium/magnesium salts remain soluble, whereas soap forms an insoluble scum with hard water.

 

NOTE

 

• Esterification (Option A): The reverse process — formation of an ester from an alcohol and a carboxylic acid.

 

• Hydrogenation (Option B): The addition of hydrogen to unsaturated compounds (e.g. converting vegetable oil to vegetable ghee) using a nickel catalyst, unrelated to esters and NaOH.

 

• Acidification (Option D): Not a standard term for this reaction; treating an ester with an acid instead of a base gives acid hydrolysis, not saponification.

question:
If the mass of two objects is halved and the distance between them is also halved, the

gravitational force ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is remains same as before.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• By Newton's Law of Gravitation, F = G m₁m₂/r², where m₁ and m₂ are the masses and r is the distance between their centres. (गुरुत्वाकर्षण नियम)

 

• If both masses are halved, the product m₁m₂ becomes (m₁/2)(m₂/2) = m₁m₂/4, i.e. the numerator becomes one-fourth.

 

• If the distance is halved, r² becomes (r/2)² = r²/4, i.e. the denominator also becomes one-fourth. Since both numerator and denominator reduce by the same factor (1/4), they cancel out, and the new force = (m₁m₂/4) ÷ (r²/4) = m₁m₂/r² = F, the same as before.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• The universal gravitational constant G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg², and it has the same value everywhere in the universe, independent of the medium.

 

• Gravitational force is directly proportional to the product of the masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance — this is called an inverse-square law, also followed by electrostatic (Coulomb) force.

 

• Gravitational force is always attractive, unlike electrostatic force, which can be attractive or repulsive.

 

NOTE

 

• Becomes double (Option A): Would be true only if, say, distance were halved while masses stayed the same (giving F × 4, not ×2); it does not match this combined change.

 

• Becomes one-fourth as much (Option B): Would result if only the masses were halved (numerator ÷4) with distance unchanged — not the case here since distance is also halved.

 

• Becomes half as much (Option C): Does not follow from the inverse-square relationship for the given combined changes in mass and distance.

question:
To buy a car, Taniya borrowed ₹75,000 at 8% per annum simple interest for 27 months.

How much interest will she pay?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. ₹13,500.

 

GIVEN

 

• Principal P = ₹75,000; Rate R = 8% per annum; Time = 27 months.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Convert time to years: 27 months = 27/12 years = 9/4 years.

 

• Simple Interest = (P × R × T)/100 = (75,000 × 8 × 9/4)/100.

 

• = (75,000 × 8 × 9) / (4 × 100) = 5,400,000 / 400 = ₹13,500.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Find interest per year first: 8% of 75,000 = ₹6,000/year. For 27 months (2 years + 3 months): 2 × 6,000 + (3/12) × 6,000 = 12,000 + 1,500 = ₹13,500.

 

NOTE

 

• Always convert the given time into years before applying SI = PRT/100; a common mistake is forgetting to divide months by 12.

question:
A dealer marks his goods at 80% above the cost price and allows a discount of 5% on

the marked price. What is his gain or loss percentage?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 71% gain.

 

GIVEN

 

• Marked price = Cost price + 80% of cost price. Discount allowed = 5% on marked price.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let cost price (CP) = 100. Marked price (MP) = 100 + 80% of 100 = 180.

 

• Discount = 5% of 180 = 9. Selling price (SP) = 180 − 9 = 171.

 

• Gain = SP − CP = 171 − 100 = 71. Gain% = (71/100) × 100 = 71% gain.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Net effect of a mark-up of x% followed by a discount of y% (on the marked price): Net % = x − y − (xy/100) = 80 − 5 − (80×5)/100 = 75 − 4 = 71% gain.

 

NOTE

 

• Take CP = 100 for such mark-up/discount questions — it converts every step directly into a percentage and avoids fraction errors.

question: The least value of x, so that the number 73318x4 is divisible by 8 is
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 2.

 

GIVEN

 

• Number = 73318x4, and it must be divisible by 8.

 

SOLUTION

 

• A number is divisible by 8 if the number formed by its last three digits is divisible by 8. Here the last three digits are '8x4'.

 

• Test x = 1: 814 ÷ 8 = 101.75 (not divisible). Test x = 2: 824 ÷ 8 = 103 exactly (divisible!).

 

• Since x = 2 already works and we need the least value, check if any smaller digit (0 or 1) works: 0→804÷8=100.5 (no); 1→814÷8=101.75 (no). So the least value that works is x = 2.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For divisibility by 8, only check the last 3 digits of the number — ignore everything before them. Just test x = 0,1,2,... in ascending order on '8x4' until one divides evenly by 8.

 

NOTE

 

• Divisibility by 8 depends only on the last three digits; divisibility by 4 depends only on the last two digits, and by 2 on the last one digit.

question:
A number is first decreased by 35% and then further decreased by 25%. By what

percentage has the original number been decreased altogether?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 51.25%.

 

GIVEN

 

• A number is decreased successively by 35% and then by 25%.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let the original number = 100. After a 35% decrease: 100 × (1 − 0.35) = 100 × 0.65 = 65.

 

• After a further 25% decrease on 65: 65 × (1 − 0.25) = 65 × 0.75 = 48.75.

 

• Total decrease = 100 − 48.75 = 51.25, so the overall percentage decrease = 51.25%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For two successive percentage changes of −a% and −b%, net change % = −a − b + (ab/100) = −35 − 25 + (35×25)/100 = −60 + 8.75 = −51.25% (i.e. a 51.25% decrease).

 

NOTE

 

• Successive percentage changes are never simply additive; always apply the second percentage on the new (reduced) value, not on the original number.

question:
A rectangular garden is 50 m long and 40 m wide. A path of uniform width is laid inside

the garden along its boundary. If the area of the path is 344 m², find the perimeter of the

inner rectangle.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 164 m.

 

GIVEN

 

• Outer garden: 50 m × 40 m. A path of uniform width w runs along the inside boundary, with path area = 344 m².

 

SOLUTION

 

• Inner rectangle dimensions = (50 − 2w) and (40 − 2w). Area of path = Outer area − Inner area.

 

• 344 = (50 × 40) − (50 − 2w)(40 − 2w) = 2000 − [2000 − 180w + 4w²] = 180w − 4w².

 

• So 4w² − 180w + 344 = 0 ⇒ w² − 45w + 86 = 0. Solving: w = [45 ± √(2025 − 344)]/2 = [45 ± √1681]/2 = [45 ± 41]/2.

 

• w = 43 (rejected, too large for a 40 m wide garden) or w = 2 m. Inner rectangle = (50 − 4) × (40 − 4) = 46 × 36.

 

• Perimeter of inner rectangle = 2 × (46 + 36) = 2 × 82 = 164 m.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Set up path area = 180w − 4w² directly from 2w(50+40−2w) and solve the quadratic; always discard the root that makes a side length negative or unrealistically large.

 

NOTE

 

• The path 'along the boundary inside the garden' reduces each side by 2w (width w removed from both ends), not just w.

question:
The cost of a washing machine is 10% less than the cost of a TV. If the cost of the

washing machine increases by 55% and that of the TV decreases by 71%, then what is

the percentage change in the total cost of 6 washing machines and 3 TVs?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. Increase by 10%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Washing machine cost = 10% less than TV cost. Washing machine price increases by 55%; TV price decreases by 71%. Find % change in total cost of 6 washing machines + 3 TVs.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let TV cost = ₹100, so washing machine cost = 90% of 100 = ₹90.

 

• Original total cost = 6 × 90 + 3 × 100 = 540 + 300 = ₹840.

 

• New washing machine price = 90 × 1.55 = ₹139.5; New TV price = 100 × 0.29 = ₹29.

 

• New total cost = 6 × 139.5 + 3 × 29 = 837 + 87 = ₹924.

 

• Change = 924 − 840 = 84. Percentage change = (84/840) × 100 = 10% increase.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Assume convenient round values (TV = 100) so the washing machine cost becomes a clean 90; this keeps every subsequent percentage calculation simple.

 

NOTE

 

• Always compute the combined 'before' and 'after' totals directly rather than averaging the two individual percentage changes, since the quantities (6 vs 3) and base prices differ.

question:
Aaron is 5 years younger than Ron. Four years later from now, Ron will be twice as old

as Aaron. Find Ron's present age.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 6 years.

 

GIVEN

 

• Aaron = Ron − 5 (present ages). Four years from now, Ron's age = 2 × Aaron's age.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let Ron's present age = R, so Aaron's present age = R − 5.

 

• Four years later: Ron = R + 4, Aaron = R − 5 + 4 = R − 1.

 

• Given: R + 4 = 2(R − 1) ⇒ R + 4 = 2R − 2 ⇒ 4 + 2 = 2R − R ⇒ R = 6.

 

• Check: Ron = 6, Aaron = 1. Four years later: Ron = 10, Aaron = 5, and 10 = 2 × 5 ✓.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Frame both ages in terms of one variable (Ron's present age) using the given age difference, then translate 'twice as old' directly into a linear equation and solve.

 

NOTE

 

• Always verify the answer by substituting back into both original conditions — it catches sign errors in 'younger/older' and 'later/ago' quickly.

question: If cotA = 3/4, the find the value of 3sin2A − cos3A is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 477/125.

 

GIVEN

 

• cot A = 3/4.

 

SOLUTION

 

• With cot A = adjacent/opposite = 3/4, take a right triangle with adjacent = 3, opposite = 4, hypotenuse = √(3²+4²) = 5. So sin A = 4/5, cos A = 3/5.

 

• sin 2A = 2 sinA cosA = 2 × (4/5) × (3/5) = 24/25, so 3 sin2A = 72/25 = 360/125.

 

• cos 3A = 4cos³A − 3cosA = 4×(27/125) − 3×(3/5) = 108/125 − 225/125 = −117/125.

 

• 3sin2A − cos3A = 360/125 − (−117/125) = 360/125 + 117/125 = 477/125.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever cotA (or tanA) is given as a ratio, immediately build the 3-4-5-type right triangle to read off sinA and cosA directly — it avoids repeated use of identities.

 

NOTE

 

• Remember the triple-angle formula cos3A = 4cos³A − 3cosA; a sign slip here (writing +3cosA) is the most common mistake in such questions.

question:
In a △MNR, the sides MN and MR are extended to P and Q, respectively.

The bisectors of ∠PNR and ∠QRN intersect at a point X.

If ∠X = 75°, then the value of 2∠M is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 60°.

 

GIVEN

 

• In △MNR, sides MN and MR are extended to P and Q. The bisectors of the exterior angles ∠PNR (at N) and ∠QRN (at R) meet at X, with ∠X = 75°.

 

SOLUTION

 

• X, the intersection of the external bisectors of angles N and R, is the excentre opposite M, and for any triangle the angle at this excentre is given by ∠X = 90° − (∠M)/2.

 

• Substituting: 75° = 90° − (∠M)/2 ⇒ (∠M)/2 = 90° − 75° = 15° ⇒ ∠M = 30°.

 

• Therefore, 2∠M = 2 × 30° = 60°.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Memorise the standard result: if the external bisectors of two angles of a triangle meet, the angle between them = 90° − (half the third angle). Apply it directly instead of deriving it from scratch.

 

NOTE

 

• Do not confuse this with the case of internal bisectors of the two base angles meeting, where the angle formed is 90° + (half the third angle) instead.

question:
What is the average speed of a car that covers half the distance at the speed of 84 km/hr

and the other half at the speed of 63 km/hr?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 72 km/hr.

 

GIVEN

 

• Half the distance covered at 84 km/hr, the other half at 63 km/hr.

 

SOLUTION

 

• For equal distances covered at two different speeds, average speed = (2 × s1 × s2)/(s1 + s2), the harmonic mean of the two speeds.

 

• Average speed = (2 × 84 × 63)/(84 + 63) = (2 × 5292)/147 = 10584/147 = 72 km/hr.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For two equal-distance legs, use the direct formula 2xy/(x+y) instead of assuming a distance and computing time — it's faster and less error-prone.

 

NOTE

 

• Average speed for equal distances uses the harmonic mean; only for equal times does the simple arithmetic mean of the speeds apply.

question: A person saves 60% of his income. If his expenditure is ₹480, then his income (in ₹) is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 1200.

 

GIVEN

 

• Savings = 60% of income, so expenditure = 40% of income = ₹480.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let income = I. Expenditure = (100 − 60)% of I = 40% of I = 480.

 

• 0.40 × I = 480 ⇒ I = 480/0.40 = 1200.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Expenditure% + Savings% = 100%; here expenditure = 40% = 480, so 100% (income) = 480 × (100/40) = 1200.

 

NOTE

 

• A common slip is computing 60% of 480 instead of recognising that 480 itself represents the 40% (expenditure) portion, not the savings portion.

question: The sides of a triangle are 146 cm, 96 cm, and 110 cm. What is its area (in cm²)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 5280 cm².

 

GIVEN

 

• Triangle with sides a = 146 cm, b = 96 cm, c = 110 cm.

 

SOLUTION (Heron's Formula)

 

• Semi-perimeter s = (146 + 96 + 110)/2 = 352/2 = 176 cm.

 

• s − a = 176 − 146 = 30; s − b = 176 − 96 = 80; s − c = 176 − 110 = 66.

 

• Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)] = √(176 × 30 × 80 × 66).

 

• Group conveniently: 176 × 30 = 5280, and 80 × 66 = 5280. So Area = √(5280 × 5280) = 5280 cm².

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• After computing s(s−a), s(s−b) or similar products, look for a pairing that gives a perfect square — here 176×30 exactly equals 80×66, making the square root immediate.

 

NOTE

 

• Always double-check that s − a, s − b, s − c are all positive before proceeding — a negative value signals the sides cannot form a valid triangle.

question:
Aditya can do 1/6th of a piece of work in 13 days and Bhagawan can do 1/9th of the same work in 12 days. Find the

number of days taken to complete the work if both work together.

(Round off your answer to one decimal place.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 45.3 days (approx.).

 

GIVEN

 

• Aditya does 1/6 of the work in 13 days. Bhagawan does 1/9 of the work in 12 days.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Time for Aditya to finish the whole work alone = 13 × 6 = 78 days, so Aditya's 1-day work = 1/78.

 

• Time for Bhagawan to finish the whole work alone = 12 × 9 = 108 days, so Bhagawan's 1-day work = 1/108.

 

• Combined 1-day work = 1/78 + 1/108. LCM(78, 108) = 1404, so = 18/1404 + 13/1404 = 31/1404.

 

• Time taken together = 1404/31 = 45.29... ≈ 45.3 days, matching Option B.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• First convert 'x/y of the work in d days' to 'whole work in (d × y/x) days' for each person — here that's simply d × (denominator/numerator) — then combine using 1/T = 1/T1 + 1/T2.

 

NOTE

 

• Don't confuse 'Aditya does 1/6 of the work in 13 days' with 'Aditya finishes the work in 13 days' — the fraction of work done must first be scaled up to the full job.

question:
A class of 95 students took a Physics test. 47 students had an average score of 93. The

other students had an average score of 54. What is the average score (rounded off to

one decimal place) of the whole class?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 73.3 (approx.).

 

GIVEN

 

• 95 students total; 47 students averaged 93; the remaining students averaged 54.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Remaining students = 95 − 47 = 48.

 

• Total score of first group = 47 × 93 = 4371. Total score of second group = 48 × 54 = 2592.

 

• Total score of whole class = 4371 + 2592 = 6963.

 

• Average of whole class = 6963/95 = 73.294... ≈ 73.3, matching Option C.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Weighted average = (sum of all individual totals) ÷ (total number of students); always find the number of students in the *second* group by subtraction before computing its total.

 

NOTE

 

• Never average 93 and 54 directly (that gives 73.5) — the two groups have unequal sizes (47 vs 48), so a straight average of the two given averages is not valid here.

question:
A vendor offers her customers a discount of 15% on her beauty products and she still

makes a profit of 5%. What is the cost price (in ₹) of a beauty product marked at ₹273?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. ₹221.

 

GIVEN

 

• Marked price = ₹273; discount = 15%; resulting profit = 5% (on cost price).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Selling price = Marked price − 15% discount = 273 × (1 − 0.15) = 273 × 0.85 = ₹232.05.

 

• Since profit = 5% on cost price: Selling price = Cost price × 1.05.

 

• Cost price = 232.05 / 1.05 = ₹221.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Chain the two percentage factors directly: CP = MP × (1 − discount%) / (1 + profit%) = 273 × 0.85/1.05 = 221.

 

NOTE

 

• Selling price is always calculated from the marked price using the discount; cost price is then found from the selling price using the profit percentage — keep the two steps separate.

question:
Determine the largest number that divides both 1058 and 1550, leaving remainders of 5

and 11, respectively.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 81.

 

GIVEN

 

• A number divides 1058 leaving remainder 5, and divides 1550 leaving remainder 11.

 

SOLUTION

 

• The required number exactly divides (1058 − 5) = 1053 and (1550 − 11) = 1539.

 

• The required number is the HCF of 1053 and 1539.

 

• 1539 = 1 × 1053 + 486; 1053 = 2 × 486 + 81; 486 = 6 × 81 + 0. So HCF = 81.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• 'Largest number dividing with given remainders' always means: subtract each remainder from its number first, then find the HCF of the results — never take HCF of the original numbers directly.

 

NOTE

 

• Quick check: 1058 ÷ 81 = 13 remainder 5 ✓, and 1550 ÷ 81 = 19 remainder 11 ✓ — always verify by division once you find the HCF.

question: If the third proportional of 50 and 30 be x, then what is the value of x?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 18.

 

GIVEN

 

• Third proportional of 50 and 30 is x.

 

SOLUTION

 

• For numbers a, b, the third proportional x satisfies a : b = b : x, i.e. b² = a × x.

 

• Here a = 50, b = 30: 30² = 50 × x ⇒ 900 = 50x ⇒ x = 900/50 = 18.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Third proportional of a and b = b²/a. Directly compute 30²/50 = 900/50 = 18.

 

NOTE

 

• Don't confuse 'third proportional of a, b' (= b²/a) with 'mean proportional of a, b' (= √(ab)) — they are different concepts.

question:
Walking at 3/4th of his normal speed from his home, Bhavesh is 15 minutes late in reaching his office.

The usual time taken by him to cover the distance between his home and his office is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 45 minutes.

 

GIVEN

 

• Bhavesh walks at 3/4 of his normal speed and is 15 minutes late.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Since speed and time are inversely proportional for a fixed distance, if speed becomes 3/4, time becomes 4/3 of the usual time.

 

• Let usual time = t minutes. New time = (4/3)t. Extra time taken = (4/3)t − t = t/3.

 

• Given extra time = 15 minutes: t/3 = 15 ⇒ t = 45 minutes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• If speed becomes a/b of the usual speed, extra time = usual time × (b/a − 1). Here (4/3 − 1) = 1/3 of usual time equals 15 min, so usual time = 45 min.

 

NOTE

 

• Speed and time for a fixed distance are always inversely proportional — a reduced speed fraction (3/4) inverts directly to a time multiplier (4/3).

question: A number when doubled and increased by 7 becomes 29. Find the number.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 11.

 

GIVEN

 

• A number, when doubled and then increased by 7, equals 29.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let the number = x. Given: 2x + 7 = 29.

 

• 2x = 29 − 7 = 22 ⇒ x = 22/2 = 11.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Translate the sentence directly into an equation in the order given (double, then add) and solve by reversing the operations: subtract 7, then divide by 2.

 

NOTE

 

• Check by substitution: 2 × 11 + 7 = 22 + 7 = 29 ✓.

question: If A : B = 1 : 3, B : C = 4 : 3 and C : D = 5 : 7, then A : B : C : D is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 20 : 60 : 45 : 63.

 

GIVEN

 

• A : B = 1 : 3, B : C = 4 : 3, C : D = 5 : 7.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Combine A:B and B:C by matching the value of B: A:B = 1:3 = 4:12 (×4); B:C = 4:3 = 12:9 (×3). So A:B:C = 4:12:9.

 

• Now combine with C:D = 5:7 by matching C: A:B:C = 4:12:9 = 20:60:45 (×5); C:D = 5:7 = 45:63 (×9).

 

• So A : B : C : D = 20 : 60 : 45 : 63.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Chain ratios by matching the common term's LCM at each step (LCM of B-values, then LCM of C-values) — this avoids fractions entirely.

 

NOTE

 

• Always scale the *whole* combined ratio (not just the new term) by the multiplying factor at each stage, to keep all four terms consistent.

question: If α+β=14 and αβ=20, then what is the value of (α²+β²)^(1/2)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 2√39.

 

GIVEN

 

• α + β = 14, αβ = 20.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Use the identity α² + β² = (α + β)² − 2αβ = 14² − 2(20) = 196 − 40 = 156.

 

• Required value = (α² + β²)^(1/2) = √156.

 

• √156 = √(4 × 39) = 2√39.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever α+β and αβ are given, α²+β² can always be found instantly via (α+β)² − 2αβ — memorise this identity for quick use.

 

NOTE

 

• Simplify square roots by pulling out the largest perfect-square factor (156 = 4×39) rather than leaving an unsimplified radical or a decimal approximation.

question:
One pipe can fill a tank in 6 minutes while another pipe can empty the completely filled

tank in 24 minutes. If both the pipes are opened together when the tank is empty, how

many minutes will it take to fill one-fourth of the tank?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 2 minutes.

 

GIVEN

 

• Filling pipe: fills the tank in 6 minutes. Emptying pipe: empties a full tank in 24 minutes. Both opened together on an empty tank.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Filling pipe's rate = 1/6 tank/min. Emptying pipe's rate = −1/24 tank/min.

 

• Combined rate = 1/6 − 1/24 = 4/24 − 1/24 = 3/24 = 1/8 tank per minute.

 

• Time to fill 1/4 of the tank = (1/4) ÷ (1/8) = (1/4) × 8 = 2 minutes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Combine rates with a minus sign for the outlet pipe, then divide the required fraction of the tank by the net rate directly — no need to find the time for the whole tank first.

 

NOTE

 

• Always express 'fills in x minutes' and 'empties in y minutes' as rates (1/x and −1/y) before adding — never subtract the times themselves.

question: Rohit bought a bicycle for ₹3,200 and sold it for ₹3,840. What is his profit percentage?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 20%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Cost price (CP) = ₹3,200; Selling price (SP) = ₹3,840.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Profit = SP − CP = 3,840 − 3,200 = ₹640.

 

• Profit% = (Profit/CP) × 100 = (640/3,200) × 100 = 20%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• 640 is exactly 1/5 of 3,200, and 1/5 = 20% — spotting such clean fractions avoids long division.

 

NOTE

 

• Profit or loss percentage is always calculated on the cost price, never on the selling price, unless the question explicitly states otherwise.

question:
The points scored by a basket-ball team in a series of matches are as follows:

17, 2, 7, 27, 25, 5, 14, 18, 10, 24, 10, 8, 7, 10.

The value of mode is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 10.

 

GIVEN

 

• Data set: 17, 2, 7, 27, 25, 5, 14, 18, 10, 24, 10, 8, 7, 10.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Mode is the value that occurs most frequently in the data set.

 

• Count frequencies: 10 appears three times (positions 9, 11, 14); 7 appears twice (positions 3, 13); every other value (17, 2, 27, 25, 5, 14, 18, 24, 8) appears only once.

 

• Since 10 has the highest frequency (3), the mode = 10.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Scan the list and tally repeated values only — single occurrences can be ignored entirely since the mode must be a value that repeats at least twice.

 

NOTE

 

• Mode is the most frequently occurring value, unlike mean (average of all values) or median (the middle value when arranged in order) — don't mix up the three.

question: Simplify: 3 × 2 + 12 ÷ (6 − 2) × 2
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 12.

 

GIVEN

 

• 3 × 2 + 12 ÷ (6 − 2) × 2 = ?

 

SOLUTION (VBODMAS: Bracket → ×/÷ (left to right) → +/−)

 

• Solve the bracket first: (6 − 2) = 4.

 

• Now perform division and multiplication from left to right: 12 ÷ 4 = 3, then 3 × 2 = 6. Also, 3 × 2 = 6 (the first term).

 

• Expression becomes: 6 + 6 = 12.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• After clearing brackets, handle all × and ÷ strictly left to right (they have equal priority) before doing any addition — a common error is doing all multiplications before all divisions regardless of order.

 

NOTE

 

• Always apply VBODMAS — Vinculum, Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction — with ×/÷ and +/− each evaluated strictly left to right within their tier.

question:
If + means −, − means ×, × means ÷ and ÷ means +, then what will come in place of the

question mark (?) in the following equation?

221 − 5 ÷ 47 + 842 × 2 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 731.

 

GIVEN

 

• Symbol swap: + means −, − means ×, × means ÷, ÷ means +. Equation: 221 − 5 ÷ 47 + 842 × 2 = ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Replace every symbol with its new meaning: − → ×, ÷ → +, + → −, × → ÷.

 

• Expression becomes: 221 × 5 + 47 − 842 ÷ 2.

 

• Apply standard BODMAS on the new expression: 842 ÷ 2 = 421; 221 × 5 = 1105.

 

• 1105 + 47 − 421 = 1152 − 421 = 731.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• First rewrite the whole expression with the substituted symbols before calculating anything — solving symbol-by-symbol while reading often causes mix-ups.

 

NOTE

 

• After substitution, apply normal order of operations (division/multiplication before addition/subtraction) on the new symbols, not the original ones.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

1001 1000 997 992 985 ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 976.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 1001, 1000, 997, 992, 985, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Find the differences between consecutive terms: 1001−1000=1; 1000−997=3; 997−992=5; 992−985=7.

 

• The differences form the odd number pattern 1, 3, 5, 7, so the next difference = 9.

 

• Next term = 985 − 9 = 976.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever consecutive differences increase by a constant step (here +2 each time, giving odd numbers), the next difference is simply the last difference + that step.

 

NOTE

 

• Always compute differences (not ratios) first for number series that look close together in value — an arithmetic pattern in the differences is very common.

question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information

given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly

known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the

statements.

Statements:

All patties are cake.

All cakes are samosa.

Conclusions:

(I): Some samosas are cake.

(II): All patties are samosa.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. Both conclusions (I) and (II) follow.

 

GIVEN

 

• Statements: All patties are cake. All cakes are samosa.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'All cakes are samosa' is a universal affirmative (A-type) statement; by simple conversion, an A-type statement always yields 'Some samosas are cake' — so Conclusion I follows.

 

• Two universal statements in the chain 'All patties are cake' and 'All cakes are samosa' combine by syllogism (A + A = A) to give 'All patties are samosa' — so Conclusion II follows.

 

• Since both conclusions logically follow from the given statements, the answer is 'Both conclusions (I) and (II) follow'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Chain 'All A are B' + 'All B are C' always gives 'All A are C' (and hence also 'Some C are A' or 'Some C are B') — memorise this standard syllogism combination.

 

NOTE

 

• Solve purely on the logical structure of the statements, ignoring whether the statement content (patties, cake, samosa) matches real-world facts.

question:
Six people, L, M, N, O, P and Q, are sitting in a straight line facing towards north. N is

sitting at the leftmost end of the row. Only 3 people are sitting between N and Q. L is

sitting second right to P. M is sitting second right to L. Based on the given arrangement

three of the following four are alike, find the odd one out?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. OP.

 

GIVEN

 

• Six people L, M, N, O, P, Q in a line facing north; N is at the leftmost end (position 1); only 3 people sit between N and Q; L is second right of P; M is second right of L.

 

SOLUTION

 

• N is at position 1. 'Only 3 people between N and Q' places Q at position 5 (positions 2, 3, 4 lie between them).

 

• P, L, M must be placed with L = P + 2 and M = L + 2 = P + 4, using the remaining positions {2, 3, 4, 6}.

 

• Taking P = 2 gives L = 4 and M = 6, which fits the available positions; the last remaining position, 3, goes to O.

 

• Final arrangement: N(1), P(2), O(3), L(4), Q(5), M(6).

 

• Now check each pair's position gap: LM = 6−4 = 2 (L before M by 2); NO = 3−1 = 2 (N before O by 2); PL = 4−2 = 2 (P before L by 2) — all three show 'first letter, then second letter 2 seats later'. OP = O(3), P(2): here the second letter P actually comes before O, breaking the pattern.

 

• So LM, NO, PL are alike; OP is the odd one out.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Once the seating is fixed, write down each person's position number and compare each option pair's order and gap — the odd one usually has a reversed order compared to the rest.

 

NOTE

 

• Fix the two most specific clues (fixed position of N, and the 'people between' clue) before working out the flexible clues (second-right relations) — it narrows the possibilities fastest.

question:
What will come in the place of '?' in the following equation, if '+' and '−' are

interchanged and '×' and '÷' are interchanged?

67 – 13 ÷ 104 × 26 + 93 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 26.

 

GIVEN

 

• Symbol swap: '+' and '−' interchanged; '×' and '÷' interchanged. Equation: 67 − 13 ÷ 104 × 26 + 93 = ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Replace symbols with their swapped meanings: − → +, ÷ → ×, × → ÷, + → −.

 

• Expression becomes: 67 + 13 × 104 ÷ 26 − 93.

 

• Apply BODMAS: 104 ÷ 26 = 4; 13 × 4 = 52.

 

• 67 + 52 − 93 = 119 − 93 = 26.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Rewrite the entire expression with swapped symbols first, then solve using normal operator precedence — never swap and calculate simultaneously.

 

NOTE

 

• '+ and − interchanged' and '× and ÷ interchanged' are two independent swaps; make sure both are applied to every relevant symbol in the expression.

question:
Refer to the given series and answer the question that follows. All numbers are single

digit numbers only. Counting to be done from left to right.

(Left) 3 2 5 4 6 2 5 3 9 7 4 5 1 1 1 5 2 3 3 8 8 4 4 6 3 1 6 (Right)

How many such even numbers are there, each of which is immediately preceded by an

odd number and also immediately followed by an odd number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 3.

 

GIVEN

 

• Sequence: 3 2 5 4 6 2 5 3 9 7 4 5 1 1 1 5 2 3 3 8 8 4 4 6 3 1 6.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Scan every even number and check both its immediate neighbours; it must be odd–even–odd.

 

• Position 2 (value 2): neighbours are 3 (odd) and 5 (odd) — qualifies.

 

• Position 11 (value 4): neighbours are 7 (odd) and 5 (odd) — qualifies.

 

• Position 17 (value 2): neighbours are 5 (odd) and 3 (odd) — qualifies.

 

• All other even numbers (positions 4, 5, 6, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24) fail because at least one neighbour is also even. Total qualifying = 3.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Underline every even digit first, then check only its immediate left and right neighbours for an odd-even-odd sandwich — don't re-scan the whole series for each digit.

 

NOTE

 

• The very first and very last terms of the series can never qualify, since they don't have both a left and a right neighbour.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

12,23,45,78,122 ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 177.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 12, 23, 45, 78, 122, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Differences between consecutive terms: 23−12=11; 45−23=22; 78−45=33; 122−78=44.

 

• The differences increase by 11 each time (11, 22, 33, 44), so the next difference = 44 + 11 = 55.

 

• Next term = 122 + 55 = 177.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Once the differences reveal a clean multiple pattern (here, multiples of 11), the next difference is just one more multiple of that base number.

 

NOTE

 

• Always list out the successive differences explicitly rather than guessing a ratio pattern — here the series is additive, not multiplicative.

question:
Pritika ranked 12th from the top and 26th from the bottom in his class. How many

students are there in the class?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 37.

 

GIVEN

 

• Pritika's rank from top = 12; rank from bottom = 26.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total students = (Rank from top) + (Rank from bottom) − 1 (Pritika is counted once in each rank, so subtract the overlap).

 

• Total = 12 + 26 − 1 = 37.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Formula to remember directly: Total students = Rank from top + Rank from bottom − 1.

 

NOTE

 

• Forgetting to subtract 1 (double-counting the person's own position) is the most common mistake in this type of question.

question:
SDVT is related to WIAX in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the

same way, IXPJ is related to MCUN. To which of the given options is UMEV related,

following the same logic?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. YRJZ.

 

GIVEN

 

• SDVT → WIAX, and IXPJ → MCUN follow the same hidden logic; find UMEV's related cluster.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check letter-by-letter position shifts for SDVT → WIAX: S(+4)=W; D(+5)=I; V(+5, wrapping)=A (22+5=27→1=A); T(+4)=X. Pattern: +4, +5, +5, +4.

 

• Verify with IXPJ → MCUN: I(+4)=M; X(+5, wrapping)=C (24+5=29→3=C); P(+5)=U; J(+4)=N. Same pattern +4, +5, +5, +4 confirmed.

 

• Apply the same shifts to UMEV: U(21)+4=25=Y; M(13)+5=18=R; E(5)+5=10=J; V(22)+4=26=Z.

 

• Result = YRJZ.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• With 4-letter clusters, always test the outer letters (1st, 4th) and inner letters (2nd, 3rd) separately — symmetric shift patterns (like +4,+5,+5,+4 here) are common.

 

NOTE

 

• Remember to wrap around using mod 26 when a shift crosses past Z back to A (e.g., V+5 → A, X+5 → C).

question:
Dhanya starts from Point A and drives 9 km towards south. She then takes a left

turn, drives 11 km, turns left and drives 2 km. She then takes a left turn and drives

4 km. She takes a final right turn, drives 7 km and stops at Point P. How far

(shortest distance) and towards which direction should she drive in order to reach

Point A again?

(Note: All turns are 90° turns only unless specified.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 7 km towards west.

 

GIVEN

 

• Start at A, facing south. Drive 9 km south, then a sequence of left/right 90° turns with given distances, ending at P.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Take north = +y, east = +x, A = (0,0). Facing south, drive 9 km → (0, −9).

 

• Left turn while facing south → now facing east; drive 11 km → (11, −9).

 

• Left turn while facing east → now facing north; drive 2 km → (11, −7).

 

• Left turn while facing north → now facing west; drive 4 km → (7, −7).

 

• Right turn while facing west → now facing north; drive 7 km → (7, 0) = P.

 

• P = (7, 0) and A = (0, 0): P is 7 km directly east of A (same y-coordinate). So from P, Dhanya must travel 7 km towards west to reach A.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Plot each leg on a simple x-y grid tracking direction changes (Left = 90° counter-clockwise, Right = 90° clockwise) — this avoids losing track of the current facing direction in multi-turn problems.

 

NOTE

 

• The final answer only needs the straight-line (shortest) distance and direction from the last point back to the start, not the total path retraced.

question:
Ayush ranked 28th from the top and 46th from the bottom in his class. How many

students are there in his class?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 73.

 

GIVEN

 

• Ayush's rank from top = 28; rank from bottom = 46.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total students = Rank from top + Rank from bottom − 1 = 28 + 46 − 1 = 73.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Directly apply: Total = (rank from top) + (rank from bottom) − 1, without needing to list out any positions.

 

NOTE

 

• This is the same formula and question type as an earlier question in this paper (Pritika's ranks) — recognising the pattern saves time.

question:
