Refer to the following number and symbol series and answer the question that follows.

Counting to be done from left to right only.

(Left) 3 % * 2 @ & 5 1 @ 6 7 1 6 # # £ 8 8 # $ £ € (Right)

How many such numbers are there, each of which is immediately preceded by a number

and also immediately followed by a symbol?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 3.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 3 % * 2 @ & 5 1 @ 6 7 1 6 # # £ 8 8 # $ £ €.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Number the positions 1 to 22 and check each numeral: does the term just before it also a number, and the term just after it a symbol?

 

• Position 8 (value 1): preceded by position 7 (5, a number) ✓, followed by position 9 (@, a symbol) ✓ — qualifies.

 

• Position 13 (value 6): preceded by position 12 (1, a number) ✓, followed by position 14 (#, a symbol) ✓ — qualifies.

 

• Position 18 (value 8): preceded by position 17 (8, a number) ✓, followed by position 19 (#, a symbol) ✓ — qualifies.

 

• All other numerals fail this exact number-before, symbol-after condition. Total qualifying = 3.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Mark every number in the series first, then check only its immediate left and right neighbours in one pass — don't re-scan the full sequence repeatedly.

 

NOTE

question:
What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if '+' and '−'

are interchanged and '×' and '÷' are interchanged?

141 ÷ 8 + 384 × 2 − 43 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 979.

 

GIVEN

 

• Symbol swap: '+' and '−' interchanged; '×' and '÷' interchanged. Equation: 141 ÷ 8 + 384 × 2 − 43 = ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Replace symbols: ÷ → ×, + → −, × → ÷, − → +.

 

• Expression becomes: 141 × 8 − 384 ÷ 2 + 43.

 

• Apply BODMAS: 141 × 8 = 1128; 384 ÷ 2 = 192.

 

• 1128 − 192 + 43 = 936 + 43 = 979.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Rewrite the expression fully with the swapped operators before evaluating anything, to avoid mixing old and new operator meanings mid-calculation.

 

NOTE

 

• Multiplication/division are evaluated before addition/subtraction even after the symbol swap — the swap changes which symbol means what, not the underlying rules of BODMAS.

question:

question:
Town M is to the east of Town N. Town O is to the south of Town M. Town P is to the

west of Town O. Town Q is to the north of Town P. Town N is to the north-west of Town

Q. What is the location of Town M with respect to Town Q?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. North-east.

 

GIVEN

 

• M is east of N; O is south of M; P is west of O; Q is north of P; N is north-west of Q.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Take M = (0, 0). N is west of M: N = (−2, 0) (using consistent but unequal step sizes to satisfy all clues).

 

• O is south of M: O = (0, −2). P is west of O: P = (−1, −2). Q is north of P: Q = (−1, −1).

 

• Check: N = (−2, 0) is indeed north-west of Q = (−1, −1), since N's x is smaller (west) and y is larger (north) — this confirms the coordinate assignment is consistent.

 

• Now compare M = (0, 0) with Q = (−1, −1): M's x (0) > Q's x (−1) → M is east of Q; M's y (0) > Q's y (−1) → M is north of Q.

 

• Combined, M is north-east of Q.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Assign simple coordinates step by step following each direction clue in order, then just compare the final x and y values of the two towns in question — no need to draw an elaborate diagram.

 

NOTE

 

• Use unequal step sizes for different legs of the journey where needed, so that the last given constraint (here, 'N is north-west of Q') is satisfied exactly — this validates your coordinate assignment.

question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information

given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly

known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the

statements.

Statements:

All hotels are restaurants.

All restaurants are cafes.

Some restaurants are kitchens.

Conclusions:

(I) Some cafes are kitchens.

(II) Some hotels are kitchens.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. Only conclusion (I) follows.

 

GIVEN

 

• Statements: All hotels are restaurants. All restaurants are cafes. Some restaurants are kitchens.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'Some restaurants are kitchens' (I-type) combined with 'All restaurants are cafes' (A-type) gives, by syllogism (I + A = I-type conclusion), 'Some cafes are kitchens' — so Conclusion I follows.

 

• 'Some restaurants are kitchens' does not specify *which* restaurants are kitchens — they need not be the same restaurants that are hotels. So we cannot conclude 'Some hotels are kitchens' — Conclusion II does not follow.

 

• Hence only Conclusion I follows.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Combining 'Some A are B' with 'All B are C' validly gives 'Some A are C' (particular + universal = particular), but combining 'Some B are C' with 'All A are B' does not validly give 'Some A are C' — the 'some' portion may not overlap with A.

 

NOTE

 

• A frequent trap in syllogisms: assuming that a 'some' relationship applies to every subgroup mentioned in a chain — it only applies to the specific overlapping portion stated.

question:
Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-clusters are

alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which letter-cluster DOES NOT belong to

that group?

(Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their

position in the letter-cluster.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. OMM.

 

GIVEN

 

• Clusters: XUV, OMM, LIJ, TQR.

 

SOLUTION

• LIJ: L(12)→I(9) = −3, I(9)→J(10) = +1. TQR: T(20)→Q(17) = −3, Q(17)→R(18) = +1.

 

• OMM: O(15)→M(13) = −2, M(13)→M(13) = 0. This does not match the (−3, +1) pattern shown by the other three.

 

• So XUV, LIJ, TQR form the group with pattern (−3, +1); OMM is the odd one out.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert each cluster to alphabet position numbers and note the gap between consecutive letters — a consistent gap pattern across three clusters quickly reveals the odd one.

 

NOTE

 

• The question explicitly rules out consonant/vowel-count-based grouping, so focus only on the numeric alphabet-position gaps between letters.

question:

are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which letter-cluster pair DOES NOT

belong to that group?

position in the letter-cluster.)
solution_text:

• RM→PT: R(18)→P(16) = −2; M(13)→T(20) = +7.

question:
C, D, E, G, H, I and J are sitting around a circular table facing the centre of the table.

Only two people sit between E and G when counted from the left of G. C sits third to the

left of J. D sits to the immediate right of J. D sits second to the left of E. I is not an

immediate neighbor of C. Who sits third to the right of H?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. D.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 people C, D, E, G, H, I, J sit around a circular table facing the centre.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Take clockwise = 'right' direction. D is immediate right of J: D = J+1.

 

• D is second to the left of E, so E = D+2 = J+3.

 

• Only 2 people between E and G counting from the left of G means E is 3 seats to the left of G, i.e. E = G−3, so G = E+3 = J+6.

 

• C is third to the left of J: C = J−3 (= J+4, mod 7).

 

• Positions used (relative to J=0): J=0, D=1, E=3, G=6, C=4. Remaining offsets {2, 5} go to H and I.

 

• Since I is not an immediate neighbour of C (offset 4; neighbours are offsets 3 and 5), I cannot be at offset 5, so I=2 and H=5.

 

• Final arrangement (offsets from J=0): J=0, D=1, I=2, E=3, C=4, H=5, G=6.

 

• Third to the right of H (offset 5): 5+3 = 8 mod 7 = 1 = D.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Fix one person as a 0 reference and express every clue as an offset from them; this converts all the 'left/right of X' clues into simple modular arithmetic.

 

NOTE

 

• Be consistent throughout about which rotational direction (clockwise or counter-clockwise) represents 'right' — mixing conventions mid-solution is the most common source of error in circular arrangement puzzles.

question:

are single-digit numbers only). Counting to be done from left to right only.

(Left) 1 8 2 9 7 6 2 4 8 3 4 6 1 9 4 2 7 4 3 5 9 8 3 5 2 4 8 (Right)

How many such even digits are there, each of which is immediately preceded by an

even digit and also immediately followed by an even digit?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. Three.

 

GIVEN

 

• Sequence: 1 8 2 9 7 6 2 4 8 3 4 6 1 9 4 2 7 4 3 5 9 8 3 5 2 4 8.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check each even digit's immediate neighbours for an even-even-even sandwich.

 

• Position 7 (value 2): neighbours are position 6 (6, even) and position 8 (4, even) — qualifies.

 

• Position 8 (value 4): neighbours are position 7 (2, even) and position 9 (8, even) — qualifies.

 

• Position 26 (value 4): neighbours are position 25 (2, even) and position 27 (8, even) — qualifies.

 

• All other even digits fail because at least one neighbour is odd. Total qualifying = Three.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

question:
M, N, O, P, W, X and Y are sitting around a circular table facing the centre of the table.

O sits to the immediate right of P. Only three people sit between O and Y when counted

from the left of O. Only three people sit between P and N when counted from the left of

P. W sits to the immediate right of M. How many people sit between X and M when

counted from the left of M?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. Two.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 people M, N, O, P, W, X, Y sit around a circular table facing the centre.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Take clockwise = 'right' direction, and P = 0. O is immediate right of P: O = 1.

 

• Only 3 between O and Y counting from the left of O means Y = O − 4 = 1 − 4 = −3 ≡ 4 (mod 7).

 

• Only 3 between P and N counting from the left of P means N = P − 4 = 0 − 4 = −4 ≡ 3 (mod 7).

 

• Positions used so far: P=0, O=1, Y=4, N=3. Remaining offsets {2, 5, 6} for M, W, X, with W = M+1.

 

• Testing M=5 gives W=6 (valid, both in remaining set), leaving X=2. (M=2 gives W=3, already taken by N — invalid; M=6 gives W=0, taken by P — invalid.)

 

• Final arrangement (offsets from P=0): P=0, O=1, X=2, N=3, Y=4, M=5, W=6.

 

• Counting from the left of M (offset 5): M−1=4(Y), M−2=3(N), M−3=2(X). So X is reached after passing 2 people (Y and N) — 2 people sit between X and M.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Solve all the fixed 'immediate right/left' and 'X between A and B' clues first using one consistent reference point, and only test the remaining free positions (like M/W here) last.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Only three people between A and B counted from the left of A' places B exactly 4 seats to the left of A (3 people + B), not 3 seats — a very common off-by-one mistake.

question:
In the following triads, each group of letters is related to the subsequent one following a

certain logic. Select from the given options, the one which follows the same logic.

INFO - NFIO - OFNI

OATH - ATOH - HTAO
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. REST - ESRT - TSER.

 

GIVEN

 

• Pattern examples: INFO → NFIO → OFNI, and OATH → ATOH → HTAO.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Step 1 (word1 → word2): rotate the first three letters one place to the left, keep the 4th letter fixed. INFO(I,N,F,O) → N,F,I,O = NFIO ✓. OATH(O,A,T,H) → A,T,O,H = ATOH ✓.

 

• Step 2 (word1 → word3): the third word is simply the full reverse of the first word. INFO reversed = OFNI ✓. OATH reversed = HTAO ✓.

 

• Apply to REST: rotate first three letters (R,E,S) left by one → E,S,R, keep T: ESRT ✓ matches given word2.

 

• Reverse REST fully: T,S,E,R = TSER ✓ matches given word3.

 

• Both transformations match exactly, so REST-ESRT-TSER follows the same logic.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Test the simplest hypothesis first — full reversal for the 1st-to-3rd word jump is easy to spot and instantly rules out three of the four options that don't reverse to their third word.

 

NOTE

 

• Verify a suspected pattern using both given example pairs before applying it to the options — a rule that fits only one example may not be the true rule.

question:
In a certain code language,

A + B means 'A is the sister of B',

A @ B means 'A is the brother of B',

A - B means 'A is the wife of B',

and A # B means 'A is the father of B'.

How is O related to V if 'O + P @ T # G - V'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. Wife's father's sister.

 

GIVEN

 

• '+' = sister of; '@' = brother of; '−' = wife of; '#' = father of. Expression: O + P @ T # G − V.

 

SOLUTION

 

• O + P: O is the sister of P. P @ T: P is the brother of T. So O and P and T are all siblings, with O female and P male.

 

• T # G: T is the father of G, so T is male, and G is T's child.

 

• G − V: G is the wife of V, so V is G's husband.

 

• O is the sibling (sister) of T, and T is G's father — so O is G's father's sister, i.e. G's paternal aunt.

 

• Since G is V's wife, O (G's father's sister) is exactly V's wife's father's sister.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Draw a quick family tree from left to right as you decode each symbol one at a time — visualising the relationships prevents errors in longer chained-relation puzzles.

 

NOTE

 

• Always work out the final relationship strictly from the perspective of the person named last in the question (here, V), tracing the chain back to O.

question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of

the following sets.

(Note: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down

the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as

adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3

and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

(24 , 12, 2)

(70, 5, 14)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. (32, 16, 2).

 

GIVEN

 

• Reference sets: (24, 12, 2) and (70, 5, 14).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check the relation between the numbers in each reference set: 24 ÷ 12 = 2 (matches the third number). 70 ÷ 5 = 14 (matches the third number).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

NOTE

 

• The question explicitly disallows digit-breaking operations, so only whole-number operations (like direct division here) are valid — don't try splitting numbers into individual digits.

question: What does the term 'Blue Washing' refer to as per the News reports in 2025?

Additional Information

question:

• The Act renamed the earlier 'Waqf Act, 1995' framework and introduced changes such as inclusion of non-Muslim members in Waqf Boards/Council, and mandatory verification of Waqf property claims.

 

• The passage of the Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2025, in Parliament was accompanied by significant political debate and was subsequently challenged in courts by various parties.

 

NOTE

 

• Section 4B (Option A): Not the section dealing with protection of women's inheritance rights under the Act.

 

• Section 2C(2) (Option B): Does not correspond to the inheritance-protection provision.

 

• Section 9F (Option D): Not the relevant section for this specific safeguard.

question:
As reported by Feeding India (an NGO) in June 2025, the big fat Indian wedding is

quietly triggering a climate chaos by adding which of the following gases in the

atmosphere?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Methane.

• A June 2025 report by Feeding India (an NGO working on food wastage and hunger) highlighted that large-scale Indian weddings contribute significantly to food wastage, and this wasted food, when it decomposes (often in landfills), releases substantial amounts of methane (CH₄) — a potent greenhouse gas. (मीथेन — भोजन अपव्यय से उत्सर्जन)

 

• Methane is far more effective at trapping heat than carbon dioxide over a short time frame (about 25-80 times more potent over 20-100 years), making food-waste-driven methane emissions a serious, though often overlooked, contributor to climate change.

 

• The report drew attention to the enormous scale of food wastage at Indian weddings, calling for better planning, portion control and food-donation practices to reduce this hidden climate impact.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Feeding India, a Zomato-backed NGO, works to combat hunger and reduce food wastage across India through food redistribution and awareness campaigns.

 

• Landfills are among the largest anthropogenic sources of methane emissions globally, since decomposing organic waste in low-oxygen conditions produces methane.

 

• India has committed to reducing its overall greenhouse gas emissions intensity and has joined the Global Methane Pledge framework discussions to curb methane emissions.

 

NOTE

 

• Hydrofluorocarbons (Option A): Greenhouse gases mainly from refrigerants and air-conditioning, not directly linked to food waste decomposition.

 

• Nitrous Oxide (Option B): A greenhouse gas mainly associated with agricultural fertiliser use, not specifically wedding food wastage.

 

• Carbon Monoxide (Option C): A toxic gas mainly from incomplete combustion (vehicles, fires), not the gas highlighted in this specific report.
